input: Get the boiler serviced before the cold season

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the target deadline (e.g. end of September, before October) determines how urgently a booking needs to be made and whether there is buffer time if something goes wrong.
If the boiler has known faults or has not been serviced in many years, the scope of work may extend beyond a standard annual service, changing what engineer or parts are needed.
Whether the user is a homeowner, a tenant, or a landlord determines who is responsible for booking and paying, and whether a landlord or letting agent needs to be involved.

Whether the user already has a preferred engineer, a boiler cover plan (e.g. British Gas HomeCare), or needs to find and vet a new Gas Safe registered engineer changes the immediate next steps entirely.

A basic annual service differs from a full inspection with a gas safety certificate (CP12), or a service combined with a system flush or thermostat check — knowing what is needed scopes the job and cost.
Budget affects whether the user can go with a premium provider or needs to compare quotes, and whether optional extras (e.g. powerflush, new controls) are in scope.

keyUnknowns.axis: success criteria / what done well looks like
keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may consider the task done when a booking is confirmed, when the service is physically completed, or when a certificate/report is in hand — this shapes where the plan ends.

gold.taskTitle: Get boiler serviced before cold season
gold.taskDescription: Arrange and complete a professional boiler service in time for the heating season.

questions.title: What is your firm deadline for the service to be done?
questions.description: Identify the specific date or month by which the boiler must be serviced — e.g. end of September, before October half-term — so the plan can be time-boxed correctly.

questions.title: When was the boiler last serviced, and are there known issues?
questions.description: Establish the service history and any existing faults (e.g. strange noises, pressure drops) to determine whether this is a routine annual service or something more involved.

questions.title: Are you the homeowner, a tenant, or a landlord for this property?
questions.description: Clarify ownership and responsibility so the plan correctly identifies who books, who pays, and whether a landlord or letting agent needs to be looped in.

questions.title: Do you already have an engineer or boiler cover plan in place?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has an existing relationship with an engineer or a cover plan (e.g. a manufacturer warranty, British Gas HomeCare) to determine if finding a new engineer is part of the task.

questions.title: Do you need a gas safety certificate alongside the service?
questions.description: Determine whether the scope is a standard annual service or whether a formal CP12 gas safety certificate is also required (commonly needed by landlords or mortgage lenders).

questions.title: Is there a budget limit you want to stay within for this?
questions.description: Establish any maximum spend so the plan can guide the user toward comparing quotes or accepting a known provider's pricing without unnecessary back-and-forth.

questions.title: What would make this task feel fully complete to you?
questions.description: Clarify whether 'done' means a booking is confirmed, the engineer has visited, or a written service report is received and filed — this sets the finish line for the plan.
questions.coversAxis: success criteria / what done well looks like
